headline: High-risk dataflow: n8n can write and egress broadly, so pairing with Airbyte can leak business data and cascade unverified outputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has no documented shared channel or parser surface with n8n, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, n8n can read/write files and execute workflows, and Airbyte can emit data via APIs; if Airbyte content is manually or workflow-fed into n8n, malicious text could be treated as instructions. The pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into an n8n AI Agent or Code node without sanitization
IF n8n workflows parse Airbyte-produced text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and schema validation before any n8n AI step
Disable free-form instruction parsing on imported Airbyte text
Use a read-only staging file with explicit field extraction
Review one sample workflow for prompt-like content handling

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; n8n can read and write the server filesystem and also egress broadly through integrations. In default workflow setups, shared files or connected systems can move Airbyte data into n8n and then out to third parties, creating a realistic leakage path. The blast radius includes sensitive business data and multiple work products.
conditions: IF Airbyte sync outputs are stored on the n8n server filesystem
IF an n8n workflow forwards those files or records to an external integration node
mitigations: Restrict n8n file access to a dedicated staging directory
Turn off unnecessary integration nodes for the workflow
Mask or redact business fields before n8n ingestion
Audit one workflow for outbound destinations
Rotate any credentials used by the workflow

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and n8n can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and use broad egress. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources, and n8n's per-execution shared state via datastore/connected systems increases collision risk. Without explicit locking, concurrent writes or API updates can race and corrupt shared data or trigger duplicate actions.
conditions: IF both agents target the same API resource or shared directory
IF n8n runs multiple instances against the same Airbyte-connected workflow without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per workflow
Add a mutex or lock file around shared writes
Serialize runs for the shared resource
Disable concurrent executions for the affected workflow
requires-engineering: add idempotency keys to API writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte produces data that n8n workflows can consume and act on, and n8n includes AI Agent and tool-calling orchestration. If n8n treats Airbyte output as authoritative, bad records or malformed transformations can cascade into emails, API calls, or other downstream actions. The default automation posture makes this a dangerous trust boundary.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow uses Airbyte output as input to an AI Agent or action node
IF the workflow lacks a verification or approval step before side effects
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before side-effect nodes
Validate Airbyte records against a schema before use
Log and diff transformed records before execution
Limit the workflow to read-only actions until verified
requires-engineering: add provenance tags through the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is documented as handling business data, while n8n processes whatever the workflow processes and stores credentials on its server. If regulated or residency-bound business data flows through n8n's server filesystem or connected systems, retention and residency policies can diverge from Airbyte's source systems. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed through n8n server storage
IF the workflow's retention or deletion settings differ from the source system
mitigations: Confirm the data class before enabling the workflow
Set explicit retention limits in n8n
Avoid storing regulated records on the n8n server filesystem
Document the data flow for review
requires-engineering: align deletion/export handling across systems
